# Settings reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_settings_doc.py from anyps5_settings.py. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every setting the GUI offers, with AnyPS5's own default and the value this tool recommends. Sources: AnyPS5 [`docs/user/USAGE.md`](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/blob/main/docs/user/USAGE.md) and [`docs/user/INPUT_MAPPING.md`](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/blob/main/docs/user/INPUT_MAPPING.md).

Settings that the installed AnyPS5 release does not contain are greyed out in the GUI.

## Build options

Used when the game is converted. Changing them requires a new build. On the command line pass the flag to `anyps5_folder.py` (tool options: `--no-audit`, `--no-backup-output`, `--no-update`).

### Relinker

| Flag | Setting | Default | Recommended | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--to-intel` | Translate AMD-only instructions (--to-intel) | OFF | ON for Intel CPUs, OFF for AMD | Rewrites AMD-specific instructions in the game and its modules so they run on an Intel CPU. It cannot fix instructions a game generates while running; such games need an AMD CPU. **Recommended ON for Intel CPUs, OFF for AMD CPUs.** |
| `--unused-filter` | Unused import filtering (unused-filter) | 0 - keep all (safest) | 0 - keep all (safest) | How unused system-library imports are removed. 0 keeps every import (safest). 1 filters unused non-PLT imports by control-flow analysis. 2 is strict analysis that also compacts the PLT and fails on unsupported cases. |
| `--windows-gui` | No console window (--windows-gui) | OFF | OFF | Builds a Windows GUI-subsystem program. When started from Explorer its output goes to anyps5.log beside eboot.exe instead of a console. **Keep OFF while testing a game so you can see errors.** |
| `--windows-diagnostics` | Startup dependency diagnostics (--windows-diagnostics) | OFF | OFF | Adds diagnostics that report which DLL or system library fails to load at startup. **Turn ON if eboot.exe closes immediately with no message.** |

### Relinker (debug)

| Flag | Setting | Default | Recommended | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--trace-imports` | Trace system-library calls (--trace-imports) | OFF | OFF | Routes every import through the libc.prx call tracer. With APS5_TRACE_CALLS set at runtime, crash and abort reports end with the last 64 calls and the most called imports. **Debugging only; slows the game.** |
| `--trap-sdk-syscall-stubs` | Trap SDK syscall stubs (--trap-sdk-syscall-stubs) | OFF | OFF | Replaces ps5-payload-dev syscall wrapper stubs with UD2 so unused wrappers do not block relinking. A trapped wrapper that runs raises an illegal-instruction exception. **Debugging only (homebrew built with ps5-payload-dev).** |

### Relinker (advanced)

| Flag | Setting | Default | Recommended | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--windows-fixed-base` | Fixed load address (--windows-fixed-base) | unset | unset | Maps the executable at a fixed address (decimal or 0x hex, 64 KiB aligned, 0x20000-0x7fffffff0000). Only for titles that assume their image starts at an exact address, e.g. 0x400000. **Leave empty unless a title needs it (some homebrew: Ruffle, VLC, XPSemu use 0x400000).** |
| `--rpath` | System library path (--rpath) | $ORIGIN/libs | $ORIGIN/libs | Where eboot.exe looks for AnyPS5 system libraries. $ORIGIN is the folder of the executable. **Leave at $ORIGIN/libs; the tool copies libraries there.** |
| `--executable` | Extra executables (--executable) | none | none | Other executables of the title that it starts with sceSystemServiceLoadExec, relative to app0 (e.g. picker/picker.bin). Each is converted beside eboot.exe. One per line. |

### Relinker (deprecated)

| Flag | Setting | Default | Recommended | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--skip-syscall-check` | Skip syscall scan (--skip-syscall-check) | OFF | OFF | **Deprecated upstream.** Disables syscall scanning in the executable and modules. **Deprecated upstream: makes games extremely unstable. Debugging only.** |
| `--exclude-sce-module` | Exclude bundled modules (--exclude-sce-module) | none | none | **Deprecated upstream.** Excludes bundled modules by exact file name (not path). One per line. **Deprecated upstream: makes games extremely unstable. Debugging only.** |
| `--skip-sce-module` | Skip all bundled modules (--skip-sce-module) | OFF | OFF | **Deprecated upstream.** Disables bundled module processing and module directory checks. **Deprecated upstream: makes games extremely unstable. Debugging only.** |
| `--lazy-binding` | Lazy symbol binding (--lazy-binding) | OFF | OFF | **Deprecated upstream.** Binds symbols lazily instead of eagerly. Incompatible with bundled ELF modules and --trace-imports. **Deprecated upstream: makes games extremely unstable. Debugging only.** |

### Tool

| Flag | Setting | Default | Recommended | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--converter-kind` | SELF converter | auto - unwrap_self.py, else self_to_elf.py | auto - unwrap_self.py, else self_to_elf.py | Turns the game's decrypted SELF/fSELF containers (eboot.bin, *.prx) into the plain ELF files the relinker needs. unwrap_self.py is AnyPS5's own converter (github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5) and refuses encrypted files. self_to_elf.py is from github.com/julienlgy/PS5-SELF-TO-ELF and also repairs broken ELF section tables. Both are downloaded and kept up to date by the updater. **Try the other converter if the relinker rejects a converted module.** |
| tool option | Run import audit | ON | ON | After relinking, lists the system functions the game imports and whether the built libraries provide them (implemented / stub / absent). |
| `--strict-audit` | Fail the build when imports are missing | OFF | OFF | Treats absent imports or missing libraries in the audit as a build failure. |
| tool option | Keep previous build as a backup | ON | ON | Renames an existing output folder to <name>_backup_<time> instead of deleting it. **Turn OFF to save disk space (old builds are deleted).** |
| `--keep-work` | Keep temporary work files | OFF | OFF | Keeps .anyps5_work (converted eboot copy, audit inputs) for debugging. |
| tool option | Check GitHub for updates before building | ON | ON | Updates AnyPS5-main and tools from the main branch and installs a newer release's relinker and libraries when one is published. |

## Runtime settings

Environment variables the AnyPS5 libraries read when the game starts. The GUI applies them on **Play** and every build writes them to `play.bat`. On the command line: `--env NAME=VALUE`.

### Performance

| Variable | Setting | Default | Recommended | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| tool option | Game log output | Log file - fastest, recommended | Log file - fastest, recommended | Where AnyPS5's log goes while the game runs. AnyPS5 writes and flushes a line for many events (textures, file opens, threads ...); shown live in a console window this is slow on Windows and can hold the game back even when the GPU is not busy. A log file costs almost nothing and is kept for crash reports (anyps5_run.log in the build folder). **Use the console only to watch the log live while debugging.** |
| `ANYPS5_SHADER_CACHE_DIR` | Shader cache folder | unset | unset | Where recompiled shaders and the Vulkan pipeline cache are kept. Default: shader_cache beside eboot.exe. Deleting it is safe. |
| `ANYPS5_NO_SHADER_CACHE` | Disable shader cache | OFF | OFF | Disables the shader and pipeline caches; every run recompiles shaders. **Keep OFF; the cache makes later runs start and play much smoother.** |
| `APS5_NO_PIPELINE_JOURNAL` | Disable pipeline journal | OFF | OFF | Stops recording/replaying Vulkan pipelines; replay pre-builds pipelines a previous run used so they do not stutter when first reached. |
| `APS5_PIPELINE_JOURNAL_THREADS` | Pipeline journal replay threads | unset | unset | Threads that rebuild journaled pipelines while the game loads. Default: half the CPU threads. 0 records without replaying. |
| `APS5_PIPELINE_JOURNAL_ENTRIES` | Pipelines replayed | unset | unset | How many journaled pipelines are replayed (the first recorded, which a run reaches first). Default: all. |
| `APS5_PIPELINE_STORE_ENTRIES` | Resident graphics pipelines | 1024 | unset | How many graphics pipelines stay resident. |
| `APS5_PIPELINE_JOURNAL_MAX_MIB` | Pipeline journal size limit (MiB) | 1024 | unset | The journal file size at which recording stops. |
| `APS5_NO_PIPELINE_LTO` | Disable pipeline link-time optimisation | OFF | OFF | Builds pipelines without link-time optimisation. |

### Game

| Variable | Setting | Default | Recommended | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ANYPS5_LANGUAGE` | Console language | 1 - English (United States) | unset | The console language games read with sceSystemServiceParamGetInt. |
| `ANYPS5_SYSTEM_FONTS` | System fonts folder | unset | unset | Folder with console system fonts (SST-Roman.otf ...) or Noto substitutes, for games that open system font sets. Default: anyps5-fonts beside eboot.exe. |

### Display

| Variable | Setting | Default | Recommended | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ANYPS5_GPU` | GPU (part of its name) | unset | unset | Runs on the Vulkan device whose name contains this text (case-insensitive). By default the first usable device is used, preferring a discrete GPU. Names are printed at start-up in the 'Physical device candidate' lines. **Leave empty; e.g. 'NVIDIA' or '1050' forces the GeForce if the Intel GPU gets picked.** |
| `ANYPS5_PRESENT_MODE` | Present mode | fifo - vsync (default) | unset | fifo = vertical sync. fifo_latest_ready and mailbox show whole frames without making the game wait for the display. immediate presents at once and can tear. Flips stay paced at 59.94 Hz. |
| `VK_LOADER_DRIVERS_DISABLE` | Disable Vulkan drivers | unset | unset | Vulkan driver manifest names to skip. '*dzn*' disables Mesa Dozen (from the OpenCL/OpenGL/Vulkan Compatibility Pack), which can crash some D3D12 drivers during start-up. **Set to *dzn* only if the game crashes while listing GPUs and you have another Vulkan driver.** |

### Compatibility

| Variable | Setting | Default | Recommended | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `APS5_STORE_AT_FLIP` | Store GPU results at each flip | OFF | OFF | Writes every pending GPU result back to game memory when a frame is flipped. Fixes titles that reuse memory after waiting for GPU work and see it overwritten later. **Try ON if a game freezes or shows corruption after menus/scene changes (Blue Prince). Costs one write-back per pending image per frame.** |
| `APS5_STORE_AT_LABEL` | Store GPU results before each label | OFF | OFF | Writes pending GPU results back before each GPU label write, for titles that wait for a GPU label and then read results on the CPU. **Try ON if a game reads stale data after GPU work. Expensive.** |

### Diagnostics

| Variable | Setting | Default | Recommended | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `APS5_TRACE_CALLS` | Traced libraries | unset | unset | Comma-separated libraries whose calls are recorded (e.g. libkernel,libSceSaveData) or 'all'. Crash reports then list the last 64 calls. **Only works if the game was built with --trace-imports.** Requires `--trace-imports`. |
| `APS5_HANG_DUMP_SECS` | Timed hang dump (seconds) | unset | unset | After this many seconds, prints a crash report with every thread's stack and stops the game. Use it to see where a frozen game is stuck. |
| `APS5_GPU_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS` | GPU wait report (ms) | unset | unset | Reports a GPU WAIT_REG_MEM that has not completed after this many milliseconds (keeps waiting). |
| `APS5_STALL_WATCHDOG_SECS` | GPU stall watchdog (seconds) | 0 | unset | Prints the GPU submission rings when a queue makes no progress for this many seconds; the game keeps running. 0 disables. |
| `APS5_PM4_RING` | GPU submissions kept for dumps | 16 | unset | How many command-buffer submissions per GPU queue are kept for crash/stall dumps (0-4096). |
| `APS5_CRASH_INDIRECT_MEMORY` | Crash report: dump pointed-to memory | OFF | OFF | Adds up to 64 bytes from each pointer found in registers to crash reports. |
| `APS5_PROFILE_DRAW` | Draw/pipeline profiling | OFF | OFF | Prints draw and pipeline-journal statistics. |
| `APS5_PAD_INPUT_FILE` | Scripted controller input file | unset | unset | Absolute path of a command file that tools/pad_input.py writes button presses to (automated tests). |

## Controller and mouse

Controllers (Xbox / PlayStation layouts via SDL) work without any configuration. Without one, the game is played with this built-in keyboard and mouse layout; keys only reach the game while its window is active. Change any of them in the window (*Controller & mouse* tab: **Set...** / **Add...**), which writes `anyps5-input.ini` beside `eboot.exe`.

### Default keyboard and mouse layout

| PS button | Default key / mouse |
|---|---|
| ✕  Cross | Enter / Space |
| ○  Circle | C |
| △  Triangle | I |
| □  Square | Left mouse button |
| L1 | Q |
| R1 | E / Left Alt / Right Alt |
| L2 | (none) |
| R2 | Right mouse button |
| L3 (left stick click) | Left Shift / Right Shift |
| R3 (right stick click) | Left Ctrl / Right Ctrl |
| Options | Escape |
| D-pad up | Up / Mouse wheel up |
| D-pad right | Right |
| D-pad down | Down / Mouse wheel down |
| D-pad left | Left |
| Left stick left | A |
| Left stick right | D |
| Left stick up | W |
| Left stick down | S |
| Right stick left | F |
| Right stick right | H |
| Right stick up | T |
| Right stick down | G |
| Touchpad (left half) | Backspace |
| Touchpad (right half) | Tab |
| Mouse as right stick on/off | Middle mouse button |
| Fullscreen on/off | F11 |

Square has only the left mouse button and L2 has nothing by default; give them keys if a game needs them.

### Controller

| Key | Setting | Default | Recommended | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `LeftStickDeadzone` | Left stick deadzone (%) | 0 | unset | Percentage (0-90) of the controller stick's travel that reads as centred. |
| `RightStickDeadzone` | Right stick deadzone (%) | 0 | unset | Percentage (0-90) of the controller stick's travel that reads as centred. |

### Mouse as right stick

| Key | Setting | Default | Recommended | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `MouseSensitivity` | Mouse sensitivity | 1 | unset | Above 0, at most 10. A larger number needs less mouse movement for full stick tilt. |
| `MouseVerticalScale` | Mouse vertical scale | 1 | unset | 0.1-10, multiplies vertical mouse speed. |
| `MouseCurve` | Mouse response curve | 1 | unset | 0.2-5. Above 1 gives finer control at low speed; below 1 reaches large tilts sooner. |
| `MouseDeadzoneOffset` | Mouse minimum tilt | 0.2 | unset | 0-0.9, the smallest tilt any movement produces. Set just above the game's own deadzone. |
| `MouseMaxSpeed` | Mouse max speed | 1 | unset | 0.1-10, the highest tracked speed as a multiple of the full-tilt speed. |
| `MouseSmoothingMs` | Mouse smoothing (ms) | 10 | unset | 0-500, smoothing time constant. 0 follows every mouse report directly. |
| `MouseDecayMs` | Mouse decay (ms) | 30 | unset | 1-1000, milliseconds without movement after which the stick is centred. |

In `anyps5-input.ini` bindings are one per line, `Action = KEY:<SDL key name>`, `MOUSE:Left|Middle|Right|X1|X2` or `WHEEL:Up|Down`. The first line for an action replaces its built-in binding; further lines add alternates. Actions: `Cross`, `Circle`, `Triangle`, `Square`, `L1`, `R1`, `L2`, `R2`, `L3`, `R3`, `Options`, `Up`, `Right`, `Down`, `Left`, `LeftStickLeft`, `LeftStickRight`, `LeftStickUp`, `LeftStickDown`, `RightStickLeft`, `RightStickRight`, `RightStickUp`, `RightStickDown`, `TouchLeft`, `TouchRight`, `ToggleMouse`, `ToggleFullscreen`.

## Developer switches

The **Developer switches** tab lists every other `ANYPS5_*` / `APS5_*` variable found in the AnyPS5 source (several hundred). They are undocumented internals for AnyPS5 developers, change often, and can stop a game when set wrongly. Leave them empty unless an AnyPS5 developer asks you to set one.
